A learner must prepare CuSO4 from warm dilute H2SO4. CuO is insoluble; NaOH is soluble. Which route is appropriate?

parts.credit_requirement: Plan AgCl preparation: soluble silver salt (1), soluble chloride solution (1), mix measured quantities (1), filter precipitate (1), wash/remove soluble impurities (1), dry and judge completion/purity from observations (1).
parts.prompt: Plan a teacher-supervised preparation of a clean, dry sample of insoluble silver chloride from suitable soluble starting salts. Include measured mixing, separation, washing, drying and a practical check that precipitation is complete. Collect silver-containing waste separately.
parts.canonical_answer: Use silver nitrate solution and sodium chloride solution in measured suitable amounts. Mix with stirring to precipitate AgCl; a slight excess of chloride can be used. After settling, test a separate small clear portion with an additional drop of chloride solution: no further cloudiness supports completion of silver precipitation. Filter the main mixture and keep the white AgCl residue. Wash with small portions of distilled water to remove dissolved salts, then dry between clean filter papers or by a suitable low-temperature method while protecting from strong light. The visual completion check does not prove full purity; careful washing and uncontaminated apparatus support it.

Suitable soluble chloride (1).
Measured mixing with stated completion check (1).
Filter and retain precipitate (1).
Wash to remove soluble impurities (1).
Appropriate drying and distinguish completion evidence from proof of purity (1). Accept equivalent safe preparation; maximum six marks.
